entries.title: C0029 attempt: Gaussian hard-edge comparison, corrected finite-n scope
entries.statement: C0029 asks whether an n by n iid uniform-sign matrix B satisfies P(s_min(B) <= t/sqrt(n)) <= t + exp(-Omega(n)) with exact coefficient one for all t >= 0. The 2026-09-07 Gaussian-comparison attempt did not prove this. The curve F(t)=1-exp(-t-t^2/2) is the LIMIT of the real-Gaussian CDF P(sqrt(n) s_min(G_n) <= t) as n tends to infinity for fixed t; it is not that CDF exactly at each finite n. At n=1 the true Gaussian CDF is 2 Phi(t)-1. Tao-Vu's quantitative universality gives a polynomial probability error and settles a polynomial-scale regime; Sah-Sahasrabudhe-Sawhney obtain a (1+o(1)) coefficient with exponential remainder. Neither estimate alone supplies the exact coefficient-one bound throughout the intermediate small-ball window. Current global openness is unverified here; this is an unsuccessful attempt record, not a theorem solving C0029.
assumptions: B has iid uniform entries in {-1,+1}
G_n has iid real N(0,1) entries
The limiting Gaussian statement holds for each fixed t>=0 as n tends to infinity

entries.title: Real Gaussian hard-edge limiting CDF differs at finite n
entries.statement: Let G_n be an n by n matrix with iid real standard-normal entries. The function F(t)=1-exp(-t-t^2/2), t>=0, is the limiting CDF of sqrt(n) s_min(G_n) at each fixed t as n tends to infinity, but it is not the exact finite-n CDF for every n. Already at n=1, P(s_min(G_1)<=t)=2 Phi(t)-1 differs from F(t).
entries.proof_text: Tao and Vu Theorem 1.1 states the real-Gaussian formula with an o(1) term as n tends to infinity. At n=1, s_min([Z])=|Z| for Z standard normal, so the CDF equals P(-t<=Z<=t)=2 Phi(t)-1. Its right derivative at zero is 2 phi(0)=sqrt(2/pi), whereas F'(0)=1. Thus the two functions differ.
assumptions: all Gaussian entries are independent real N(0,1)
